video_title: LeBron James on Leaving LA and Choosing Philly

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on his high school experience at the Palestra
quotes.excerpt: I actually played at the Palestra in high school. My senior year, it was historical.
quotes.quote: I actually played at the Palestra in high school. My senior year, it was historical for us to go there. Growing up and being in a historian and reading stories about the Palestra and obviously Wilt Chamberlain and all the things that he did there and how historical it was for us to go there, my senior year, being from Akron, I was in a building with some of the greatest ever played. It just had an aura about it when I played there, it was fun.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on Maurice Cheeks breaking Wilt Chamberlain's scoring record
quotes.excerpt: We was playing the number one player in Pennsylvania, Maurice Cheeks. He broke Wilt Chamberlain's single season scoring record.
quotes.quote: We was playing the number one player in Pennsylvania, Maurice Cheeks. He broke Wilt Chamberlain's single season scoring record. I'm reading all this stuff about Wilt and the history of the game, and we're traveling to Philadelphia and they say, 'Okay, well you guys are going against the guy who's broken Wilt's single season scoring record.' And I'm like, this guy Wilt averaged 60 and 40. What the hell is this guy doing? So it was like, oh, we better have our shoes tight and we better be ready to go.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on the impact of Don Nelson on his career
quotes.excerpt: Nelly means the world to me. He's one of a kind. Larger than life, big personality.
quotes.quote: Nelly means the world to me. He's one of a kind. Larger than life, big personality, can walk into any room and own it, free spirit, but also a basketball mind and genius. The effect he had on the game, played in the league, obviously won championships, hit a game-winning shot in the finals, I think at the Forum, if I'm not mistaken, hit the back room, bounced way up in the air, went in, coached at a lead-lead level, one of the all-time leaders in wins, was on the rules committee, always out in front of where's the game going, what are we doing, how can we affect and make the game better. But for me, it was about a coach who took me at a time in my career that was tricky for me and where I was just trying to make a name for myself. I played two pretty good years in Phoenix, but was playing behind Jason Kidd, Kevin Johnson. Second year, earned a bunch of minutes, showed a little value. They thought they were going to lose me in free agency so they traded me and I went to Dallas and hurt my back. That's when I first realized I had back issues. So it was tricky at first, but playing for Nelly was amazing because he would push you, but he also believed in you. And if you could handle it, he'd give you more rope and more rope and more rope. So he challenged me in a lot of ways.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Nash on Don Nelson's coaching philosophy and aggressiveness
quotes.excerpt: He would push you, but he also believed in you. He made me more aggressive and less shy.
quotes.quote: He would push you, but he also believed in you. He made me more aggressive and less shy. I grew up in an era where the point guard was to run the team, organize the team, facilitate, and he thought that was bullshit. He's like, 'You can score the ball, you can attack. I want you to attack and shoot the ball as many times as you need to shoot the ball.' And one story that I remember, and the details maybe a little fuzzy, but we played Atlanta, I think, I came out pretty passive, maybe had like five points in the first half, we're down 20. He kind of laid into us, got on me for not being aggressive. I think I had 35 in the second half, and we lose in overtime, and he comes in the locker room and he was like, 'That's fucking bullshit. If you're a dominant player, dominate.' And he lit me up. You know, you're thinking, 'Yeah man, we lost, but got us back in the game.' He's like, 'That's unacceptable. Your job is to attack and to kill people.' And I think for me as a young player from the West Coast of Canada, someone believing like, 'You're as good as these guys. Don't sit and wait and play make, go.' And so that was impactful for me for the rest of my career to not be shy, to believe, to to know I belong.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James explains his criteria for knowing when to retire
quotes.excerpt: If I feel like I am cheating that process because that's what's got me to this point
quotes.quote: If I feel like I can't put in the process of waking up and training the body and training the mind, and I feel good after I do that on a consistent basis, if I feel like I am cheating that process because that's what's got me to this point, then I know for sure that I'm done.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on why he continues to play professional basketball
quotes.excerpt: If I have an opportunity to still do what I love to do and continue to inspire people
quotes.quote: If I still have an opportunity to do what I love, then why just say I'm done? What is the reasoning? If I have an opportunity to still do what I love to do and continue to inspire people in what I love to do, then I think that's what it came down to.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on his excitement for his new teammates
quotes.excerpt: I'm excited about that, almost more than that's going to sound crazy, but actually get on the floor.
quotes.quote: I'm excited about that, almost more than that's going to sound crazy, but actually get on the floor. Because if that thing clicks, this will be easy. That will be easy. So I'm excited and intrigued about that. And as time goes by, you know, I'm sure you get some time with the fam, you take your break, you know, you do other things. By the way, your golf game improved this summer? It has. Here we go. That's a good sign. YouTube channel. Yeah, come on, subscribe. But you go from like, everything's in doubt. Season ends, I don't know, what team, am I still playing, how do I feel about this whole thing? To what were the stages to get to like, I'm playing first? Yeah, I mean, it all came down to, you know, for me, I've always told myself like, if I feel like I can't put in the process of waking up and training the body and training the mind, and I feel good after I do that on a consistent basis, like Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, if I feel like I am cheating that process because that's what's got me to this point, then I know for sure that I'm done. And I was able to take the time off after the season, I took a month and a half, two months off of no basketball. I was still doing certain things, whatever the case may be, to try to keep the body in a good place, but yeah, I just I felt like my body responded very well after the season. My mind responded better than it actually did last summer.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on his relationship with Tyrese Maxey
quotes.excerpt: My relationship with Tyrese Maxey goes beyond the court.
quotes.quote: My relationship with Tyrese Maxey goes beyond the court. You can tell every time you mention him on the pod. You love him. And by the way, and when I mention him in the past on the on the podcast, Philly was not even in question. Like it was just like I didn't even know they were No, absolutely. I didn't even, you know, obviously and it's way before the JB trade as well, which was another intriguing piece. You know, but I I just love everything about Tyrese Maxey, man. Like, he just every every day you get the same person. And that is very rare in sports and and obviously super rare in life. And I've always talked about how great of a person that he is and obviously we know what he brings to the basketball court, but like he was definitely when I became a free agent and and we decided to let the Lakers know that I wouldn't be returning, he was one of the first people that was on my line, calling me, 'Yo, what we doing? Oh, what's up? What's up OG? What's up, what's up, old head? You know, come on down here, man. We can use you down here.' You know, so and and our relationship like it's a lot of times that I just I don't answer the phone for a lot of phone calls, because I don't even want to be swayed one way or I don't even I already know what you calling about, but I mean, he's just such a he's such a great person. I cannot not talk to him, one.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on his desire to help Tyrese Maxey win a championship
quotes.excerpt: He's done everything in our league and the only thing he has not done is win a championship.
quotes.quote: He's done everything in our league and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one. He's been MVP of our league, has a gold medal, All-Stars, signature shoes, a bunch of money, beautiful family. He has everything. He has the city on his back. It's been the process for what, 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I mean, I think it's time now that we even dig even deeper into the process and I and I and I hope that I can be kind of that final little piece that can help him get over the hump and and have him see maybe just see it a little bit differently than he's seen it in his in his career, I mean as far as like the day-to-day process, the day-to-day what it takes to to get there. So I'm I'm excited and intrigued about that.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James on the importance of pride in team defense
quotes.excerpt: defense always comes down to the first thing, like a pride. It's a pride thing.
quotes.quote: I've been able to be on some really good defensive teams in my career and I think defense always comes down to the first thing, like a pride. It's a pride thing. I'm not going to allow my guy to continue to exploit me or beat me or whatever the case may be. There has to be some type of pride in the sense of that. At the end of the day, the best defense never stops the best offense anyways. That's okay. But if we can make teams uncomfortable, if we can make teams turn the ball over, or not be in a rhythm like they're accustomed to being in a rhythm versus other teams, it gives us another opportunity. It gives us more possessions. We want to try to win the possession game.

quotes.speaker: LeBron James
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James analyzes Nick Nurse's defensive coaching philosophy
quotes.excerpt: I'm looking forward to seeing if we can kind of translate a little bit of that
quotes.quote: With Coach Nurse and the things that I've seen with his teams in the past, especially with the Raptors team that won a championship, that's what they did. They got up into you, they got into the passing lane, if you got around one guy, there's another guy helping you. With OG, Kawhi, and Pascal, and then you have the smarts of Marc, it was a lot of high IQ guys as well to be able to do that. I'm looking forward to seeing if we can kind of translate a little bit of that as well because we have the speed, we have the athleticism, now it's about do we have the discipline to actually be able to take that on a defensive end and hold each other accountable.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Defining the subjective nature of what constitutes an NBA super team
quotes.excerpt: The reality is it's not the names, it's where are they at this stage in their career.
quotes.quote: I think a super team we should probably all agree that a super team is just a collection of players and personalities that have had a lot of success, that have either been All-Stars or heliocentric parts of their team. But the reality is it's not the names, it's where are they at this stage in their career, what have they been doing. Like some people would say this is a super team and some people say that's not a super team because it's been going on for a long, long time.

quotes.speaker: Steve Nash
quotes.summary_phrase: Historical context and the difficulty of defining super teams across eras
quotes.excerpt: There's no real way to define which each team is.
quotes.quote: You've had teams with three or four, absolutely, great players. The Lakers, Celtics, you make their super teams. I mean, even teams going to the radar like the Lakers who won with Pau Gasol, Andrew Bynum, Lamar Odom, these are teams you could consider super teams, but people don't want to. There's no real way to define which each team is. Clearly some have the makings, the Warriors team where a lot of that teams have been healthy. But that's a big issue, health, age, what stage of your career you're at.
